label: Dopamine D1
claim: Prefrontal D1 is the dominant cortical DA receptor; tone follows an inverted-U — too little or too much degrades working memory.

source.title: The Signaling and Pharmacology of the Dopamine D1 Receptor

label: Dopamine D2
claim: Antipsychotic efficacy = mesolimbic D2 blockade; EPS = nigrostriatal and hyperprolactinemia = tuberoinfundibular D2 blockade.

source.title: The role of D2-autoreceptors in regulating dopamine neuron activity and transmission

label: DAT — Dopamine Transporter
claim: Methylphenidate blocks DAT; amphetamine reverses it — both raise synaptic DA.

label: Serotonin 5-HT1A
claim: 5-HT1A partial agonism is anxiolytic, reduces parkinsonism and augments SSRI/antipsychotic effect; autoreceptor desensitization underlies antidepressant delay.

label: Serotonin 5-HT2A
claim: 5-HT2A antagonism disinhibits nigrostriatal DA, reducing EPS — the basis of ‘atypicality’; agonism underlies psychedelics.

label: Serotonin 5-HT2C
claim: 5-HT2C antagonism disinhibits prefrontal DA/NE (antidepressant) but drives weight gain.

source.title: The 5-HT2C receptor and antipsychotic-induced weight gain — mechanisms and genetics

label: SERT — Serotonin Transporter
claim: SERT inhibition by SSRIs/SNRIs is the foundational antidepressant/anxiolytic mechanism; ~80% occupancy needed, with delayed onset.

source.title: Molecular pathways linking the serotonin transporter (SERT) to depression

label: Alpha-1 Adrenergic
claim: α1 antagonism improves PTSD nightmares (prazosin) and agitation, but causes orthostasis and sedation.

label: Alpha-2 Adrenergic
claim: Postsynaptic α2A agonism (guanfacine, clonidine) strengthens prefrontal connectivity; presynaptic α2 antagonism (mirtazapine) boosts NE/5-HT.

label: Beta-1 (β1) Adrenergic
claim: Central β role in psychiatry is limited; propranolol is used for performance/somatic anxiety and akathisia.

source.title: Polymorphic variants of adrenoceptors: pharmacology, physiology

label: NET — Norepinephrine Transporter
claim: NET inhibition (atomoxetine, SNRIs, TCAs) raises NE — and DA in prefrontal cortex (sparse DAT) — treating ADHD/depression.

source.title: Norepinephrine Reuptake Inhibition, an Emergent Treatment…

label: NMDA Glutamate Receptor
claim: NMDA hypofunction is a leading model of schizophrenia’s negative/cognitive symptoms; ketamine (high-affinity) vs memantine (low-affinity) open-channel block differ clinically.

source.title: Structure, function, and allosteric modulation of NMDA receptors

label: Histamine H1
claim: Central H1 antagonism causes sedation and weight gain (olanzapine, quetiapine); peripheral effects underlie antihistamine use.

source.title: International Union of Basic and Clinical Pharmacology: Histamine receptors

label: Muscarinic M1
claim: M1 agonism (xanomeline) is procognitive/antipsychotic; M1 blockade causes anticholinergic effects but can reduce EPS.

source.title: Muscarinic acetylcholine receptors: novel opportunities for drug discovery

label: μ-Opioid Receptor (MOR)
claim: MOR full agonism (morphine), partial agonism (buprenorphine), and antagonism (naloxone) span analgesia, OUD treatment, and reversal.

source.title: Mu Opioid Pharmacology: 40 Years to the Promised Land
